suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-17 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited systematic review found that irritable bowel syndrome is frequently comorbid with psychiatric disorders, especially major depression and anxiety, without establishing onset order or direction. Require independently established irritable bowel syndrome and a separately established depressive disorder; the cited systematic review reported frequent comorbidity of irritable bowel syndrome with major depression and anxiety and does not establish onset order or direction. Preserve other functional gastrointestinal disorders, visceral hypersensitivity, infectious or inflammatory bowel disease, medications, substance use, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from gastrointestinal symptoms, distress, or impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that irritable bowel syndrome caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
